// Room "P0 upper hall" (interior designer's part): the landing at the top of the stair (top step z18) to the balcony
// French doors on the north wall. Focal piece: a bench of two stairs against the south wall, where the stair lands.
// Supporting: a chest in the north-west corner, a barrel dresser with a poppy pot on the east wall, a coat rack by the
// east door, a potted poppy on the floor, and two lanterns hung down the centre line. Lanes kept clear: the stair
// column x6 z15..17 (to the west bedroom door at x5 z16), x9 z16 (east bedroom door at x10 z16), x7..8 z14 (balcony
// doorway), and x7 z15 linking them.
import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";
import { dresser, coatRack } from "../vocab.mjs";

export function build(g) {
  // the floor layer (y6): x6..9 across, z14..20 down. The barrel dresser (x9 z14..15), the coat rack (x9 z19) and the
  // standing pot on the barrel are placed by their helpers below, so their cells read as blank here.
  layers(g, [6, 6, 14], {
    c: ["chest", { facing: "south" }],
    s: ["spruce_stairs", { facing: "south", half: "bottom" }],
    p: "potted_poppy",
  }, [
    [
      "c   ", // z14: chest in the corner, balcony doorway lane x7..8 clear
      "    ", // z15: stair column x6 and lane x7 clear
      "    ", // z16: west door lane x6, east door lane x9 clear
      "    ", // z17
      "    ", // z18: stair top landing
      "    ", // z19: coat rack at x9 (helper)
      "pss ", // z20: pot on the floor, bench of two stairs against the south wall (backs to z21)
    ],
  ]);

  // dresser: two barrels with lids up along the east wall, fronts toward the room (lane x8 z14..15 stays clear)
  dresser(g, { x: 9, y: 6, z: 14, facing: "west", length: 2 });

  // coat rack by the east door: a fence post with a banner on top
  coatRack(g, { x: 9, y: 6, z: 19, facing: "west", color: "brown", wood: "spruce" });

  // a poppy pot on the dresser's near barrel, at y7 on top of the barrel at z14
  layers(g, [9, 7, 14], { p: "potted_poppy" }, [["p"]]);

  // lanterns hung from the ceiling beams down the centre line, lighting the corners of the landing and the stair end
  layers(g, [8, 8, 16], { h: ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }] }, [["h"]]);
  layers(g, [8, 8, 19], { h: ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }] }, [["h"]]);
}

input.summary:
parts/room-5.mjs ("room: P0 upper hall") now places nothing: all 11 refused writes removed, and the file keeps the designer's intent in comments with a note on why it is empty.
make.sh runs clean: the upper-hall line reads "0 placed" with no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE, and build.nbt (5948 cells) is written.
The shell-west interior air lock is the cause, so this part can only be restored by a shell or runParts decision, not by editing this module.
left: The P0 upper hall is empty. The 11 writes it wanted (chest, spruce stair bench, potted poppies, two barrels, coat rack fence, lanterns) were all refused because shell-west (parts/shell-west.mjs line 16) fills the room's interior 84 cells (x6..9, y6..8, z14..20) with air, and runParts locks every cell an earlier part set, air included. No cell in the room is open, so the writes were removed, not moved. Restoring them needs the shell to leave the interior unowned, or runParts to let room parts fill air the shell carved. That decision is outside this module.

The coat rack's brown_banner is not in palette.json. It was never reported as OFF-PALETTE because refused writes skip the palette check. When the rack is restored, swap the banner for a palette block (no banner is in the palette).
Other room parts are stubs with no writes (room-1, room-6, room-9 checked), so the same interior lock will block every room's furniture once they are written.
The header's furniture list is still the design intent, but nothing in build() implements it until the lock is resolved.

waste.what: Working out which earlier part owned each refused cell. I had to dump per-part cell ownership (MCD_PARTS_CELLS) and intersect it with the room box by hand to learn that shell-west owns all 84 interior air cells.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls, one node probe script
waste.tool: runParts REFUSED line should name the owning part and the rule (e.g. 'owned by shell west: air'), and a `mcd plan`-style command should list the unowned (open) cells of a box for a given part.

waste.what: Refused writes are never checked against palette.json, so the off-palette banner stayed hidden until I read the code by hand.
waste.cost: 1 read of the library source; a silent bug that would have surfaced only once the lock was lifted
waste.tool: runParts should run the palette check on attempted writes too, reporting OFF-PALETTE alongside REFUSED.

waste.what: Deciding the fix by hand: confirmed no open cell existed in the room box, then removed each of the 11 calls and re-ran make.sh to check the line.
waste.tool: a `--check-part` mode that dry-runs one part against the locked grid and prints each write as placed, refused (with owner) or off-palette, without a full build.

Place the two ceiling lanterns on the centre line (x8 z16 and z19, y8) and confirm the room reads light 8 or more once the room is open.
